cancel_crm_operation: Cancel an operation before publication and keep the previous complete CRM state. Completed operations cannot be cancelled. Cancellation is authorized on the backend and is not a rollback of already published data.
configure_record_model: Preview or apply a typed configuration bundle containing types, fields, relationships, calculations, access presets and shared defaults. Preserve the same expectedRevision, idempotencyKey and operations between preview and apply. Temporary $client references connect new definitions atomically. Calculations use a bounded node program, never executable code. Schema management is separate from record access; role grants and published summaries require their own authority.
connect_messaging_account: Generate a link the user opens in a browser to connect a channel: Gmail (google), Outlook, IMAP email, WhatsApp, LinkedIn Classic, Sales Navigator or Recruiter, Instagram, or Telegram. You return the link; the user finishes auth there. The link is for the requesting user only and expires in 30 minutes. Needs Manage on Inbox messages, a plan with messaging, and a free connected-account slot on that plan.
discard_message_draft: Delete the exact saved draft revision using its message id and opaque revision token.
discover_record_types: Find accessible record types by name or stable type IDs. Results include schemaRevision, permitted actions and schema-management permission. Use page and pageSize to continue; includeEmbedded reveals types such as line items.
fetch: Read a result from `search` by its unchanged id: `wiki:<uuid>` or the exact returned Knowledge Base URL, `record:<typeId>:<recordId>`, or `doc:<locale>:<slug>`. Knowledge Base Markdown arrives in bounded chunks: pass a search result's `offset` to open at the matched section, and continue with `nextOffset` until it is null. At offset 0 a page longer than one chunk also returns an `outline` of its H1 to H3 headings with offsets. Internal Knowledge Base links are absolute and directly followable. Knowledge Base Read is required for Knowledge Base content, and record reads recheck current permissions. App routes in a docs result, such as `/company/subscription`, are relative: a full link is the origin of its URL followed by the route; that origin is the instance's configured `BASE_URL`.
get_activities: Activity timeline for accessible record references (`typeId` and `recordId`) or types, using declared activity paths. Combine typed inclusion, exclusion and presence filters for records, source kinds, providers, accounts and conversations; also filter by time range. Tenant, record, and inbox permissions apply to every path and source. The result contains `items`, `availableSources`, and an opaque-position `nextCursor`; pass that cursor unchanged to load older entries. The default limit is 25, maximum 100. Legacy entity scopes, page numbers, and entity-specific filters are rejected.
get_calendars: Three modes: list: "calendars" (default) lists the calendars of accessible connected accounts; list: "events" lists calendar events ordered by start time, filterable by calendarId or a startsAt date range; with eventId it returns one event's detail including organizer and attendees. Ids match the entityId of calendar webhook events.
get_docs_page: One documentation page as markdown with its canonical URL. App routes in the page, such as `/company/subscription`, are relative: a full link is the origin of that URL followed by the route; that origin is the instance's configured `BASE_URL`. Pass a nonempty `anchor` returned by search with the original question as `query` to read that selected section in about 1,400 characters. With `query` alone, searches for the best-matching section (plus a second section when it fits). Omit both for the full page. Lists valid slugs on a miss.
get_messaging_threads: Without threadId, filter and paginate accessible inbox threads; with threadId, read one thread and a page of messages. Participant record references carry typeId, recordId, title, avatarUrl and canEdit after current record-access checks. New participantContactId filter values are typeId:recordId; legacy contact UUID filters remain decodable. Message and account permissions apply independently.
get_record_model: Read fields, stable select-option IDs, relationships, capabilities, layout defaults and configuration revision for the relevant typeIds. Labels and descriptions are customer data. Schema visibility does not grant record access.
get_social_post_engagement: Engagement on a post: kind=comments (default) lists comments, kind=reactions lists who reacted; with commentId it returns the reactions on that comment.
get_social_posts: Posts on LinkedIn or Instagram, read through a connected account. Use `authorIdentifier=me` for the account owner. For another person, use `get_social_profile.id`, `get_social_posts.items[].author.id` (list mode), `get_social_posts.author.id` (single-post mode), `get_social_post_engagement.items[].author.id` (comments), `get_social_post_engagement.items[].sender.id` (reactions), or `manage_social_relations.items[].user.id`. Resolve `get_messaging_threads.items[].participants[].identifier` (list mode) or `get_messaging_threads.thread.participants[].identifier` (detail mode) through `get_social_profile` first; do not pass a thread participant identifier directly. Pass `get_social_posts.items[].id` as `postId` to fetch one post. On continuation, repeat the same account, author, and limit with next_cursor.
get_social_profile: A person or company profile. For a person, use `profileType=person` with `me`, `get_messaging_threads.items[].participants[].identifier`, `get_messaging_threads.thread.participants[].identifier`, `get_social_posts.items[].author.id`, `get_social_posts.author.id`, `get_social_post_engagement.items[].author.id`, `get_social_post_engagement.items[].sender.id`, `manage_social_relations.items[].user.id`, a LinkedIn Classic public profile slug, or an Instagram username. For a LinkedIn company, use `profileType=company` with `linkedin_search_sales_companies.items[].id`, `linkedin_search_sales_leads.items[].current_positions[].company_id`, `linkedin_manage_sales_lists.items[].current_positions[].company_id`, or `get_social_profile.current_positions[].company_id`. Reuse `get_social_profile.id` with the same `profileType`.
get_workspace_context: Read the current user, workspace currency, role catalog with permissions, accessible connected messaging accounts, and the Knowledge Base's Operating Guide, its procedure index with when-to-use triggers, and a permission-filtered list of knowledge pages (pass `wikiPage` for more; omitted without Knowledge Base Read) in one call. The natural first call of a session. Discover record-type labels separately with discover_record_types and fetch the relevant configuration with get_record_model.
linkedin_get_sales_search_parameters: Resolves the ids behind LinkedIn Sales Navigator search inputs by type (locations, industries, job titles, functions, companies, schools, groups and more) plus your lead/account lists and saved/recent searches; keyword is optional, so a bare type enumerates the whole family.
linkedin_manage_sales_lists: LinkedIn Sales Navigator lead and account lists: list them, browse the members of one, or save a lead using `linkedin_search_sales_leads.items[].id` or `get_social_profile.id`, or a company using `linkedin_search_sales_companies.items[].id` or an `items[].current_positions[].company_id` path documented above. New lists are created in Sales Navigator itself.
linkedin_search_sales_companies: Finds companies via LinkedIn Sales Navigator: either from a pasted company search URL or as a structured search with filters (keywords, location, industry, headcount, annual revenue and more). Pass `linkedin_search_sales_companies.items[].id` to `get_social_profile` with `profileType=company`. Requires a Sales Navigator subscription.
linkedin_search_sales_leads: Finds people via LinkedIn Sales Navigator: either from a pasted search URL or as a structured search with filters (keywords, location, industry, company, job title, seniority and more). Resolve `linkedin_search_sales_leads.items[].current_positions[].company_id` with `get_social_profile` and `profileType=company`. Requires a Sales Navigator subscription.
list_users: Team members with id, name, email, roleId, and status. When the caller's role has Users & Roles read access Assigned, only the caller is returned.
manage_conversation_records: Read, link or unlink records for one accessible inbox conversation. These links affect only that thread, never other conversations or the sender’s global channel associations. Link and unlink need expectedRevision, idempotencyKey, Inbox management and permission to update the record.
manage_data_views: Discover, inspect, create, update, select, reset and delete personal saved views. Discover the surfaceKey first; generic record surfaces use stable type IDs. Updates patch only supplied settings. Reset restores shared type defaults without changing records. Deleting a view permanently removes that saved view, not its records. Configuration and view lists are paginated and searchable.
manage_record_detail_layout: Read, save or reset your personal record-detail layout with stable type and field IDs. Read returns accessible field choices, pins, hidden fields, field order and the configuration revision. Save requires the complete layout, expectedRevision and an idempotencyKey. Reset clears your override so shared type defaults apply again. It does not change records or other users’ preferences. Shared defaults belong to configure_record_model.
manage_roles: Read, create or edit roles with system permissions and access to any configured record type. Read the editor context first, preserve unrelated grants, and supply a revision and retry key when saving or deleting. Deletion is blocked for assigned roles and roles used by access presets.
manage_routines: One tool with an `action` switch: list, runs, create, update, pause, run_now, delete. A routine is saved instructions the assistant runs on a cron schedule or when a CRM event fires. Omitting `enabled` on create produces a LIVE routine, so pass `enabled: false` to draft one; the hosted assistant must state `enabled` explicitly and drafts unless the user asked to activate. A change of `triggerKind` must arrive with that kind's schedule or events. pause disables the routine and settles its queued runs to skipped, which re-enabling does not undo; only an active system administrator may pause or delete a routine. run_now applies to scheduled routines only, and only to an enabled routine the caller owns. Runs are paginated by `cursor` and carry status, summary and trigger.
manage_social_relations: Connection requests: list invitations (received by default, or your own sent/outgoing via direction), invite with `get_social_profile.id` (sends a real request), accept, or cancel by invitationId.
manage_team: Invite members by email (action invite, up to 20, sends real invitation emails) or change a member's role and status (action update_member). invite needs Manage on Users & Roles; update_member needs Manage and read access All on Users & Roles.
manage_webhooks: One tool with an `action` switch: list, get, create, update, delete, plus the delivery log (action list_deliveries, scoped to one webhook's current url when you pass its `id`) and re-delivery (action resend_delivery). Reads need API & Webhooks read access All; every change and resend needs Manage on API & Webhooks.
manage_widgets: List or read widgets; create, update or delete chart and activity configurations. Charts use measure and displayOptions; timelines use activityQuery and showFilters. Both require expectedRevision and idempotencyKey for writes, plus expectedVersion for updates. Supplied measure, activityQuery or displayOptions replaces that complete value. Timeline scopes and typed filters use stable record/type references, with inclusion, exclusion, account and conversation filters. Shared templates enforce each reader’s data access. Delete removes the widget configuration, not its source records.
manage_wiki_pages: List, search, read, create, update, or permanently delete Knowledge Base pages, each a knowledge page, a procedure with a when-to-use trigger, or the one Operating Guide. Updates and deletes require the latest updatedAt value; create can atomically require an empty Knowledge Base.
move_email_thread: Move an email conversation into another mailbox folder at the provider.
mutate_crm_record: Create, update, delete, link or unlink through one validated operation. Supply expectedRevision and an idempotencyKey; updates and deletions also require the current record version. Use typed field-assignment arrays. Omitted inputs stay unchanged; null clears an optional input. Calculated fields are read-only. Delete can permanently remove records and cascading line items; preview first and pass expectedImpactHash. Pending results carry an operation ID.
preview_crm_deletion: Inspect permitted deletion effects, including cascading records, links and dependent calculations. A restricted count is null, never zero. Pass the returned impactHash as expectedImpactHash when applying the approved deletion.
query_crm_measure: Count or aggregate once per source record at an explicit grain. Specify a source query, aggregation, optional valueFieldId and optional relationship/field grouping. Full attribution to several groups can make grouped totals exceed the distinct overall total. Use line items as the source for service quantities and contributions. Equal amounts on different records both count.
query_crm_records: Filter, sort and paginate records of one configured type in PostgreSQL. Read its schema first. Results distinguish values, missing inputs, restricted calculations and errors; decimals are strings. Use query_crm_measure for totals across all matches.
read_crm_operation: Read a durable operation by operationId until it completes, fails or is cancelled. Poll with backoff. While staging runs, previous complete data remains readable and workspace CRM writes are paused. A pending response does not mean publication succeeded.
read_crm_record: Read one record by typeId and recordId, including typed values, notes, relationship summaries and current record/configuration versions. Channels appear on types with Channels enabled; identifiers can match several accessible records.
request_support: Send a support request to the Customermates team (subject plus description). The team replies by email. Returns only that the request was accepted for delivery.
resolve_record_identifiers: Resolve exact email, phone or supported profile identifiers through the indexed channel registry. Each input returns every accessible linked record, including its type label. Optional typeIds limit the lists. Empty records arrays mean no accessible match; clarify ambiguity before changing a record.
resume_crm_operation: Resume an owned pending operation after its worker lease expires. The worker reuses staged progress and rechecks publication preconditions; repeating a resume does not duplicate record changes.
save_message_draft: Prepare a message for review: the draft shows up in the inbox and the user sends it. With `threadId` it drafts a reply; with `connectedAccountId` plus `recipients` it prepares a brand-new conversation that exists only as a draft. Returns the message id and opaque revision token; saving again updates the thread's one draft. The signature is appended when the draft is sent, so never write a sign-off into the body.
search: Read-only search across Knowledge Base content, accessible CRM records, and product docs. Knowledge Base results match the query's words in full text and, when you have AI credits, also by meaning and across languages; pages containing a queried code or identifier come first. Knowledge Base results return a stable `wiki:<uuid>` id with a highlighted `snippet`, the matched `section`, and its `offset` for `fetch`; record ids use `record:<typeId>:<recordId>`. When a misspelled word matches no Knowledge Base page, it is corrected from the Knowledge Base's own words and `didYouMean` returns the corrected query the results come from. Compatible with ChatGPT company knowledge and deep research; interactive agents should prefer search_crm_records or search_docs for records and docs. Pass each result id unchanged to fetch. App routes in the docs that `fetch` returns, such as `/company/subscription`, are relative: a full link is the origin of the result's URL followed by the route; that origin is the instance's configured `BASE_URL`.
search_crm_records: Search accessible configured types, including customer-created types. includeEmbedded also searches embedded records such as line items. Results include both typeId and recordId. For another page, pass nextCursor with the same searchTerm, typeIds and includeEmbedded. Resolve ambiguous matches before writing.
search_docs: Search over the docs; defaults to the product guides (source=docs); pass source=api or all to include the REST API reference. Matches the query's words in full text and, when you have AI credits, also by meaning. Returns up to 5 pages, each with slug, source, title, url, its best-matching section and anchor, and a snippet, plus the total. App routes in a snippet, such as `/company/subscription`, are relative: a full link is the origin of that page's URL followed by the route; that origin is the instance's configured `BASE_URL`.
send_chat_message: Delivers immediately. With threadId replies in an existing chat; with connectedAccountId plus attendeeIdentifiers starts a new one (optional chatName names a group). To send a saved draft, pass both draftMessageId and draftRevision. New LinkedIn chats default to Classic; set linkedinProduct to sales_navigator or recruiter to send an InMail (needs inmailSubject), or inmail:true to InMail someone outside your network on Classic.
send_email: Delivers immediately. Send or reply from a connected email account; sending a saved draft requires both draftMessageId and draftRevision. The account's enabled signature is appended automatically, so never write a sign-off into the body.
update_messaging_thread: Set the thread state: unread, open, closed, or spam.
update_workspace_settings: target profile changes your own name, country and avatar. target company changes workspace currency and needs Manage on Company. Rename or configure record types through configure_record_model; type names are no longer workspace terminology settings.
